text.p: These are the highlights of the main Sao Paulo and Rio de Janeiro newspapers this morning.
-- HALF THE COUNTRY DOES NOT UNDERSTAND MERCOSUR

The Mercosur customs union is a mystery for a large portion of the Brazilian population. Half the country understands the purpose of the trade pact while the other half has no idea what the agreement is all about, according to a new Gallup poll.
-- CAPITAL FLOWS TO EMERGING MARKETS HIT NEW RECORD

Private investment in emerging markets -- which has grown steadily for the last six years -- hit a record $244 billion in 1996, up $60 billion over 1995 levels, the Inter American Development Bank reported.
-- REVENUE SERVICE PROBES THOSE INVOLVED IN BOND SCANDAL
Brazil's Internal Revenue Service has opened a probe to investigate over 30 people involved in a multi-billion dollar bond scam. -- GOVERNMENT WANTS ACTION AGAINST CHILD PROSTITUTION

Justice Ministry officials have promised to act against charges of child prostitution in Manaus after O Globo reported on Sunday that 12 year-old girls were found approaching clients in the city while nearby police turned a blind eye.
-- CONGRESSMEN TO PROBE BANK ACCOUNTS IN BOND SCANDAL
A congressional probe investigating a multi-million dollar bond scam will require 24 banks to identify the account holders of 201 cheques issued by some of those suspected of masterminding the fraud.
-- ONLY ONE CONSORTIUM WILL BID FOR VALE DO RIO DOCE
A consortium led by the Brazil's Votorantim group and Southafrica's Anglo-American will be the only bidder at the April 29 privatization auction of state mining giant Vale do Rio Doce.
-- Reuters has not verified these stories and cannot vouch for their accuracy.
